name: Greggs
news: First-half sales rose 7.2% to £1.1bn and pre-tax profit 20% to £76m, with 34 net new shops and 100 to 110 openings planned this year.

name: JD Sports
news: JD Sports plans to close about 175 Hibbett stores over three years, favouring larger formats, and expects flat organic sales growth in fiscal 2027 amid muted markets.

name: Card Factory
news: First-half revenue rose 5.3% to £260.8m but UK like-for-like sales fell 2.3%; it is merging Funky Pigeon and cardfactory.co.uk and pushing into gifts and party.

name: Pets at Home
news: James Bailey, formerly managing director of Waitrose, became chief executive on 30 March 2026 as the retailer pursues a turnaround after two profit warnings.

name: AO.com
news: AO World guided to about 11% revenue growth and profit at the top of its £45m to £50m range for the year to March 2026.

name: Dunelm
news: Dunelm reported FY26 sales of £1.83bn, up 3.1%, and launched a three-year 'Winning Hearts & Homes' strategy including app and AI shopping assistant investment.

name: Gymshark
news: Gymshark is opening its first gym, the Gymshark Lifting Club, in Miami's Wynwood district later in 2026, moving beyond apparel into in-person fitness.

name: Hobbycraft
news: Hobbycraft exited its CVA 13 months early, with online active users up 13%, three new stores opened and nine underperforming shops closed.

name: The White Company
news: Chief executive Paula Nickolds is leaving at the end of May after two years, and the retailer is searching for an interim and permanent successor.

name: Boden
news: Boden opened its second US store in Nashville and plans a third in Birmingham, Alabama this autumn; US is nearly half of group revenue.

name: Mountain Warehouse
news: Founder Mark Neale steps back to executive chair as Marcus Ward becomes chief executive on 1 September, after turnover passed £500m for the first time.

name: Moonpig
news: FY26 revenue rose 6.5% to £373m with 12.3m active customers, under new chief executive Catherine Faiers, who joined in March 2026.

name: Bloom & Wild
news: Bloom & Wild relaunched its seasonal 100% Organic Blooms bouquet from a Soil Association certified Herefordshire farm, with £1 per sale going to Rewilding Britain.

name: Gousto
news: Founder and chief executive Timo Boldt is moving to a board role after nearly 15 years, with a successor due in the first half of 2027.

name: FatFace
news: FatFace is trialling a free in-store personal styling service in six stores through summer 2026 and has added WhatsApp customer service, now 18% of contacts.

name: Seasalt Cornwall
news: Seasalt closed all four of its US stores by mid-May, shifting to wholesale partners to lift international sales from 16% to over 20% of revenue.

name: Lush
news: Lush is expanding experiential retail, launching an app feature to book in-store workshops and consultations from late April, alongside click-and-collect and its Lush Lens scanning tool.

name: Superdry
news: Superdry plans 21 new stores in 2026, 15 in the UK and six in Europe including Berlin and Utrecht, following its Superdry & Co rebrand.

name: Schuh
news: Genesco appointed Tomas Petersson, formerly of Foot Locker EMEA, as president of Schuh, replacing Colin Temple who is retiring after 38 years.

name: Innocent Drinks
news: Innocent appointed former SodaStream global CMO Sam Grant as Director of Marketing and Innovation, replacing Kirsty Hunter, as it accelerates its Fruiture strategy.

name: Fever-Tree
news: H1 revenue rose 7% to £184.2m, with US sales up 11% at constant currency after its first national US marketing campaign.

name: Pip & Nut
news: Posted its first full-year profit for 2025, with revenue up 50% to £26.4m and a post-tax profit of about £733k.

name: Rude Health
news: Launched a £1m integrated campaign running 18 months, its biggest since the 2024 Oddlygood takeover, targeting shoppers worried about ultra-processed food.

name: Graze
news: Katjes International completed its purchase of Graze from Unilever, keeping about 180 staff and aiming for roughly €100m of UK revenue this year.

name: Ella's Kitchen
news: Launched Ella's Kitchen Kids, non-HFSS Crunchy Stix and Wild Crackers for children over 18 months, with more categories promised later in 2026.

name: Huel
news: Danone agreed to buy Huel in a deal worth about €1bn, to expand its complete nutrition portfolio, subject to regulatory approvals.

name: Warburtons
news: Executive chairman and two cousins plan to step back from day-to-day running within a year, with sixth-generation family members on the board as it turns 150.

name: Taylors of Harrogate
news: Appointed Fiona Fox, formerly of Inspired Pet Nutrition, as managing director of Taylors of Harrogate, replacing Andy Brown after 17 years.

name: Princes
news: Chief executive Simon Harrison departed and Giuseppe Mastrolia, previously chief commercial officer, became interim CEO of Princes Group.

name: Cranswick
news: Full-year revenue rose 9.5% to £2.98bn and adjusted operating profit climbed 14.5% to £237m, led by poultry, gourmet and pet products.

name: Weetabix
news: Launched an 850g Crispy Minis Chocolate Chip pack, as the range grew 13% and household penetration hit a six-year high, backed by £10m masterbrand spend.

name: Grenade
news: Launched in the US from Austin, Texas, with four protein bar flavours including Oreo collaborations, sold via Amazon, GNC and Vitamin Shoppe.

name: Yeo Valley
news: Turnover rose to £424.6m but pre-tax profit fell to £4.6m, in year two of a five-year investment plan and after its first acquisition, The Collective.

name: Thatchers Cider
news: Launched its Brighter Days Call for a Better Cider summer campaign with Initials CX, a new agency relationship, using Aardman-designed visuals across on and off trade.

name: Clipper Teas
news: Ran limited-edition Wilderness Festival packs with a ticket giveaway and three festival activations, aiming to reach about 45,000 younger shoppers.

name: BrewDog
news: Now owned by Tilray after a discounted March 2026 deal, it ran a Park IPA summer push with 20,000 cans via Deliveroo.

name: Tunnock's
news: A giant Tunnock's teacake closed the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games opening ceremony, and the firm has announced a factory expansion for international demand.

name: Monzo
news: Monzo reported FY2026 revenue up 39% to £1.7bn, adjusted pre-tax profit of £172.6m and 15.2m customers, and launched in Ireland in April with Spain next.

name: Starling Bank
news: Starling posted a fifth year of profit, with £217.1m pre-tax profit on £887.4m revenue, and is pushing its Engine software platform and AI banking tools.

name: Zopa
news: Zopa reported a third straight annual profit of £44.9m and said take-up of its Biscuit current account was 40% ahead of plan, with 1.7m customers.

name: Moneybox
news: Moneybox reported 2025 revenue up 23% to £115.6m, 1.71m customers and £19bn assets, and plans to roll out AI-powered personal financial advice.

name: Nationwide
news: Nationwide will overtake Lloyds in June 2026 to run the UK's largest branch network, with 696 branches including Virgin Money sites, ahead of a Virgin rebrand from 2028.

name: Hargreaves Lansdown
news: Hargreaves Lansdown hired two Vanguard executives as chief technology officer and chief transformation officer from September 2026, following a record £100m investment commitment in FY26.

name: LV=
news: LV= protection sales fell 17.7% to £186m in the first half of 2026, though overall sales held broadly stable at £580m.

name: Admiral
news: Admiral's H1 2026 pre-tax profit fell 18% to £429.2m while customers passed 12m and Admiral Money loan balances grew 39% to £1.88bn.

name: Principality Building Society
news: Principality's half-year results showed underlying profit of £22.2m, net interest margin up to 1.27% and £33m returned to members, under CEO Iain Mansfield.

name: Coventry Building Society
news: Coventry's H1 2026 results showed underlying profit down to £183m as it integrates the Co-operative Bank, with transfer into the Society planned for early 2027.

name: Yorkshire Building Society
news: Yorkshire BS reported H1 2026 statutory profit of £181.9m, with 288,000 new savings accounts and over a quarter of new mortgages going to first-time buyers.

name: Leeds Building Society
news: Leeds BS H1 2026 profit fell to £70.7m from £104.4m and lending dropped to £2.0bn as it invests in a multi-year technology modernisation programme.

name: Skipton Building Society
news: Skipton's H1 2026 group profit fell to £110.3m from £135.1m, as estate agency arm Connells' underlying profit dropped from £24.9m to £2.0m.

name: easyJet
news: easyJet announced 18 new routes for summer 2027, including two from Bristol Airport.

name: Whitbread (Premier Inn)
news: Whitbread's Q1 FY27 group sales rose 2% to £727m, with Germany accommodation sales up 16% on new Premier Inn openings and UK up 3%.

name: Travelodge
news: Travelodge chief executive Joanna Boydell left after 13 years and CFO Ray Reidy became interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor.

name: Leon
news: Leon closed 23 company-owned restaurants through a CVA, leaving 43 open, after co-founder John Vincent bought it back from Asda and injected £2.5m.

name: Jet2
news: Jet2 reported FY26 revenue of £7.48bn and pre-tax profit of £551m, announced a £250m buyback and plans seven aircraft at Gatwick by summer 2027.

name: Mitchells & Butlers
news: Q4 like-for-like sales rose 1.4% and drink sales 3.8%, with cost headwinds expected to ease from £120m to about £95m in FY2027.

name: YHA
news: YHA is selling six hostels for £7.9m and ending leases on three more as it streamlines its 73-site network after difficult trading years.

name: Merlin Entertainments
news: Chessington has revealed a Minecraft World hotel and an Escape the Nether rollercoaster, part of Merlin's wider Minecraft theme park rollout.

name: St Austell Brewery
news: St Austell is marking its 175th anniversary in 2026 with revived classic cask ales and a new anniversary beer called 1851.

name: Hall & Woodhouse
news: Underlying pre-tax profit rose 16% to £9.3m for the year to January 2026, with brewery volumes up 4% and capital spend of £19.1m.

name: Loganair
news: Loganair will close its Southampton base from late October 2026, after cutting Inverness frequencies, citing sustained losses and rising fuel, repair and airport costs.

name: The Gym Group
news: Half-year revenue rose 10% to £133.1m and adjusted pre-tax profit 31% to £6.4m, with membership at 1 million and 20 or more openings planned.

name: Vitabiotics
news: Bain Capital agreed to buy Vitabiotics and the wider VB Group in a deal reported at around $850m to $900m, with the Lalvani family staying on.

name: Boots
news: Sycamore Partners is reportedly close to selling Boots to the Weston family for about $9bn, with a deal possible within weeks.

name: PureGym
news: Half-year revenue rose 6% to £393m and adjusted EBITDA 23%, with 728 sites, 60 openings planned this year and new CEO Alex Wood targeting Ireland.

name: Myprotein
news: Myprotein unit sales are up 60% year to date, with retail expansion and new energy drink, protein water and breakfast ranges planned for the second half.

name: Westfield Health
news: Launched Evolve, a digital platform for intermediaries to quote and manage health cash plans, with Perci Health cancer screening and neurodiversity support added.

name: Wise
news: Listed on Nasdaq on 11 May while keeping its London listing, after net revenue of $2.5bn and cross-border volume of $243bn for the year to March.

name: Trainline
news: Full-year net ticket sales rose 7% to £6.32bn, but UK consumer revenue fell 1.9% after commission cuts; profit guidance was confirmed.

name: Ocado
news: Announced up to 1,000 job cuts and £150m of savings, merging two divisions, after Kroger and Sobeys closed four North American fulfilment centres.

name: Rightmove
news: H1 revenue rose 7% to £225.8m, with agentic AI tools like Ask Rightmove lifting lead conversion, while legal claims over agent fees weigh on shares.

name: Arm
news: Unveiled the AGI CPU on 24 March, its first production silicon in 35 years, with 136 Neoverse cores on a 3nm process aimed at data centres.

name: Auto Trader
news: Full-year revenue rose 4% to £624.3m and operating profit to £392.7m, with about £500m of buybacks planned next year and retailer numbers slightly down.

name: Sage
news: Half-year underlying revenue rose 11% to £1,363m, with cloud native revenue up 25% and a £600m share buyback announced.

name: MONY Group
news: Reiterated full-year guidance after a good start to 2026 and launched version 2 of its MoneySuperMarket ChatGPT app with an AI Price Optimiser.

name: Skyscanner
news: Launched Explore with AI and a Road Trip Planner, and grew its Stays platform from 3.5 million to over 5 million properties.

name: Kainos
news: Expects to beat analyst forecasts for the year to March 2027, citing record backlog and double-digit growth in both Workday services and products.

name: McLaren
news: Plans a £450m investment at Woking and up to 1,000 new jobs, under new owner CYVN and chief executive Nick Collins, as it diversifies.

name: Pod Point
news: Pod Point has acquired UK home charger maker EO Charging, expanding its position in the domestic and commercial EV charging market.

name: JLR
news: JLR held an investor day at Gaydon on 17 June, with CEO PB Balaji setting out strategy, financial outlook and its House of Brands approach.

name: Aston Martin
news: Aston Martin posted a £154.2m first-half pre-tax loss on revenue up 38% to £628.6m, secured £550m of debt funding and is cutting up to 600 jobs.

name: Motorpoint
news: Motorpoint forecast FY26 pre-tax profit up 83% to £7.5m on retail volumes up 8%, and plans a new Leeds store opening in summer 2026.

name: National Express
news: Parent Mobico is selling its West Midlands bus business to the West Midlands Combined Authority for about £24m upfront, with completion expected in November 2026.

name: Guide Dogs
news: Its chief fundraising and marketing officer is repositioning the brand to show Guide Dogs does far more than guide dogs, and has launched a new creative platform.

name: Oxfam GB
news: Happy Hour won a three-way pitch to create Oxfam's 2026 Christmas campaign, launching in November across TV, social and radio, plus a new Christmas offering.

name: Tenovus Cancer Care
news: Its 2025/26 annual report puts financial resilience first, prioritising efficiency, partnerships and income growth to meet demand for support across Wales.

name: RSPB
news: The RSPB is consulting staff on simplifying its structure beyond the reserves, as operating costs rose from about £150m to £185m and wage costs added £2m.

name: Halma
news: Full-year revenue rose 15% to £2.58bn and adjusted profit 22% to £594.5m, with five acquisitions worth £447m plus two more since year end.

name: Wates
news: 2025 turnover reached £2.56bn with £29.2m pre-tax profit, net cash of £248m and a record £10bn forward order book under CEO Eoghan O'Lionaird.

name: Renishaw
news: Full-year revenue rose 14% to £816m and adjusted operating profit 36% to £153m, driven by semiconductor encoders and additive manufacturing, with a special dividend.

name: Spirax Group
news: First-half revenue was £863m with adjusted operating profit up 8% to £171.1m, though shares fell about 10% as full-year guidance was left unchanged.

name: Screwfix
news: Kingfisher, Screwfix's owner, said CEO Thierry Garnier is leaving to run Ahold Delhaize after a 12-month notice period, and has started recruiting a successor.

name: Toolstation
news: Toolstation UK sales grew 2.6% in H1 with Toolstation Club at 900,000 members, while Travis Perkins is discussing a sale of loss-making Benelux operations.

name: JCB
news: JCB is investing £100m in its Staffordshire HQ and opening a $1bn San Antonio factory in October, expected to create 1,500 US jobs over five years.

name: Travis Perkins
news: Half-year revenue fell 1.8% to £2,258m on weaker volumes, but net cash improved to £55m and a strategic review is exploring a Toolstation Benelux sale.

name: Croda
news: Croda's first-half sales reached £880.5m, up 4.6% organically, led by Consumer Care and Beauty Actives, with full-year organic growth guidance held at 3 to 6%.

name: Victrex
news: Victrex raised full-year profit guidance to £45m to £47m after completing a 10% workforce reduction that saves at least £10m a year.

name: Weir Group
news: Weir confirmed Jon Stanton steps down as chief executive on 1 August 2026, with Minerals division president Andrew Neilson taking over.

name: Aggreko
news: Aggreko is preparing to power the FIFA World Cup and is deploying battery-backed UPS, HVO fuel and Tier 4 Final generators at major sports events.

name: Wrightbus
news: Wrightbus is marking its 80th anniversary, has launched operations in Australia and put 14 new double-deckers on Wales' TrawsCymru network, with electric buses due in 2027.

name: ITV
news: Sky agreed to buy ITV's Media & Entertainment arm, including ITVX, for up to £1.6bn, with ITV Studios staying listed and completion expected in late 2027.

name: Channel 4
news: Channel 4 appointed Priya Dogra, previously Sky's chief advertising, group data and new revenue officer, as chief executive, succeeding interim chief Jonathan Allan.

name: Global
news: Global reported 29 million weekly listeners and a 27.5% share in Q2 2026 RAJAR, with Heart at 12.8 million and LBC at a record 3.7 million.

name: Guardian Media Group
news: The Guardian reported record revenue of £282m for the year to March 2026, with US revenue up 14% and operating losses cut to £17m from £25m.

name: Everyman Cinemas
news: Everyman reported first-half revenue up 23.9% to £70.0m across 49 venues, and flagged a delisting announcement due before the end of August 2026.

name: Hollywood Bowl Group
news: Hollywood Bowl's half-year revenue rose 9.4% to £141.5m, with 77 UK and 16 Canadian centres and three more openings planned in the second half.

name: Future plc
news: Future's half-year pretax profit fell 67% to £18.4m on weaker programmatic ad and ecommerce affiliate revenue, with a plan to unlock value from weaker assets.

name: Aardman
news: Aardman is marking its 50th anniversary with a Propstore auction of over 220 puppets and props, with proceeds funding Aardman Academy bursaries.

name: S4C
news: S4C deepened its YouTube partnership as part of a digital-first strategy, launching a Newyddion S4C channel after 1.1 million YouTube viewing hours last year.

name: STV
news: STV's 2025 profit fell 44% to £11.6m, with no dividend, an £8m cost-saving programme and news production being consolidated in Glasgow pending an Ofcom decision.
